title: Real or AI:
hook: 48% of people on a live video call thought she was human. Your next Zoom call may not be.
caption:
A new AI video model just passed a test almost no AI has passed: can you tell it's fake? 👀

Tavus' Griffin talks to you live on video. It listens, nods, laughs and even interrupts, like a real person on a call.

In their live study, 26 of 54 people (48%) thought they had talked to a human. The older system fooled under 3%.

The real takeaway: "is this person real?" is now a question for every video call you take.

Would you have spotted it? Yes or no 👇

Save this, send it to the friend who trusts every video call, and follow @aiplaybooks.daily for the AI news everyone's talking about.

checked: Griffin = Tavus' 'first Human Interaction Model', research preview; claims first video Turing test pass: https://www.tavus.io/griffin

48% figure: 26 of 54 participants believed the Griffin persona was a real person after a one-minute live call; previous system Phoenix-4.5: 1 of 41 (2.4%); company-run study: https://www.businesstoday.in/technology/artificial-intelligence/story/beyond-chatbots-tavuss-griffin-model-passes-video-turing-test-with-48-human-success-rate-559295-2026-10-03
#1 on NVIDIA's VideoFDB full-duplex video benchmark (perception + generation), per Tavus: https://www.tavus.io/griffin

A new AI video model just passed a test almost no AI has passed: can you tell it's fake?

Tavus built Griffin, an AI that sits on a live video call with you. It listens, nods, laughs and interrupts the way people do.

Then they ran a live test. After a one-minute call, 26 of 54 people (48%) believed they had talked to a real person. Their previous system fooled just 1 in 41.

youtube.title: AI video model fooled 48% of people on a live call: real or AI?
youtube.description:
An AI video model that 48% of people mistook for a real human on a live call: Tavus' Griffin and its "video Turing test".

Our take: Griffin listens, nods, laughs and interrupts in real time, and that changes what a video call proves. In Tavus' own study, 26 of 54 people thought they talked to a person after one minute; their older system fooled 1 of 41. A face on a screen is no longer proof that someone is there.

What to do: on any surprise video call about money or passwords, ask something only the real person would know.

Video: @tavus on X

#aivideo #turingtest #ai
